anomalies.observed: On the 'FCC Peripherals' sheet the Winbond W25N01GVZEIG_TR NAND flash U4 has its VCC pin (pin 8) tied to a 5 V net (the label above the pin reads as a 5 V rail, distinct from the +3.3V labels used on the same sheet for R24/R25 and the EEPROM/PWM-driver VCC pins), with only C36 100 nF as decoupling.
anomalies.expected: The W25N01GV is a 3.3 V-only part (VCC 2.7-3.6 V) and, per the design's own distribution scheme, should be powered from the 3V3 rail like the other FCC digital peripherals; the 5 V rail is reserved for servo/PWM power, the GPS and the CH330 bridges.

evidence.quote: 'U4 W25N01GVZEIG_TR ... VCC 8' connected to the 5 V net (FCC Peripherals sheet)
'3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs; 5 V feeds the servo/PWM connector bank, the GPS module, and the CH330 USB-UART bridges.'

anomalies.impact: Applying 5 V to the 3.3 V flash exceeds its absolute-maximum supply, likely destroying U4 (and/or latching up), so the FCC loses its NAND flash storage.

parsed.summary: The design is largely consistent with the specification, but the FCC-side W25N01GV flash (U4) appears to have its VCC pin tied to a 5 V net rather than the 3.3 V rail, which would over-voltage the 3.3 V-only NAND part.
